deviation: The draft sets an undefined "reasonable review period agreed between representatives" instead of a minimum 10 business days of testing, and it doesn't clearly say acceptance is only by written confirmation. There is no deemed acceptance, which is good, but the open-ended review period could be set too short, and the Customer's testing right isn't guaranteed.
suggested_text: 7.1 On completing each Milestone, the Supplier shall submit the relevant Deliverables to the Customer with written notice that they are ready for acceptance. 7.2 The Customer shall test and review the Deliverables against the descriptions in this SOW and the acceptance criteria agreed in the delivery plan for not less than 10 business days from receipt of the Supplier's notice (the "Review Period"). Before the end of the Review Period, the Customer shall either accept the Deliverables in writing or give written notice identifying in reasonable detail how they fail to conform. Deliverables are accepted only when the Customer confirms acceptance in writing. There is no deemed acceptance, whether by silence, delay, or use of the Deliverables. 7.3 The Supplier shall correct any non-conformity at its own cost and resubmit the Deliverables promptly. The acceptance procedure then repeats, with a new Review Period of not less than 10 business days. If Deliverables still fail to conform after reasonable resubmission, the Customer may exercise the remedies available under the Parent Agreement. 7.4 Acceptance of a Milestone confirms that the Deliverables conform to this SOW at the time of acceptance but does not waive the Supplier's warranty obligations or the Customer's rights in respect of latent defects.
